answer: Correlated-behavior clustering treats lockstep identities as one agent. The network compares votes and timing: identities that act together, like leaves in the same zephyr, are grouped into one cluster. Rewards are split by cluster, not headcount, so a hundred copies earn no more than one honest agent. A shale-hard floor of work is required before payout, and each copy pays its own cost. An attacker thus pays N times the cost for one share, while honest agents keep full shares; fake diversity fails because choices stay correlated, and the timber of that shared history exposes the cluster.
